section_summary: This section records the March 1949 approval and implementation of Allied policy on patents, utility models, and designs in occupied Japan, including a separate U.S. interim directive on priority for patent applications. It includes the Japanese government's account of wartime industrial property measures, SCAP's restoration procedures, and subsequent correspondence about Japanese patent applications abroad and access to patent records.

subfiles.title: Interim Directive on Patents in Japan
subfiles.about: Proposes alternate interim patent directives depending on the Far Eastern Commission’s March 17 votes.
subfiles.summary: Explains the Soviet objection to extended priority and urges prompt signature of memoranda for SANACC and General McCoy.

subfiles.title: SCAP Staff Study on Japanese Foreign Patent Applications
subfiles.about: Reviews SCAP’s proposal to permit Japanese applications abroad for inventions developed after January 1, 1946.
subfiles.summary: Recommends no action on despatch 73 pending further comment.

subfiles.title: Issuance of Interim Directive on Patent Priority
subfiles.about: Recommends directives following approval of FEC 284/17 and the Soviet veto of FEC 333/2.
subfiles.summary: Seeks signatures for the approved general patent policy and an urgent U.S. interim directive granting patent priority.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Far Eastern Commission Policy No. 56
subfiles.about: Forwards the approved policy on patents, utility models, and designs in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests notice when the directive reaches Tokyo so the policy can be released to the press.

subfiles.title: Certification of Policy No. 56
subfiles.about: Certifies the attached policy as a correct copy of the Commission’s adopted text.
subfiles.summary: Certifies the copy of Policy No. 56.

subfiles.title: Policy Toward Patents, Utility Models, and Designs in Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets occupation policy for Japan’s patent office and Allied industrial property rights.
subfiles.summary: Calls for patent publication, an end to secret patents, and restoration of Allied rights lost during the war. Owners may seek a term extension or recover royalties; provisions also apply to utility models and designs.

subfiles.title: Draft Directive on Patents, Utility Models and Designs
subfiles.about: Transmits a draft directive based on the Commission’s approved patent policy.
subfiles.summary: Requests transmission to General MacArthur and acknowledgment of SCAP’s receipt.

subfiles.title: Draft Interim Directive on Patent Application Priority
subfiles.about: Transmits an urgent draft U.S. interim directive on patent priority.
subfiles.summary: Requests Joint Chiefs of Staff transmission to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Draft Interim Directive Regarding Priority for Patent Applications in Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Grants wartime foreign applicants priority rights in Japan with safeguards for existing users.
subfiles.summary: Provides priority based on first filing and nonexclusive licenses for qualifying third parties.

subfiles.title: SCAP Telegram on Swiss Patent Royalties
subfiles.about: Reports advice to the Swiss mission about collecting royalties and seeking license agreements.
subfiles.summary: SCAP asks that the U.S. member of the Commission be informed.

subfiles.title: Statement for U.S. Member of the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Explains the U.S. interim directive on patent application priority to Commission members.
subfiles.summary: Sets out the urgency of priority protection, the failed attempt at unanimous agreement, and U.S. authority to issue an interim directive.

subfiles.title: Filing Directives Serial Nos. 100 and 101
subfiles.about: Submits memoranda for filing certified copies of two patent directives with the Commission.
subfiles.summary: Requests signatures on two filing memoranda.

subfiles.title: Statement for General McCoy
subfiles.about: Recommends informing Commission members of the U.S. patent priority interim directive.
subfiles.summary: Seeks approval of the attached notification to General McCoy.

subfiles.title: Directives Transmitted to SCAP
subfiles.about: Sends copies of patent Directives Serial Nos. 100 and 101 transmitted to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Provides four copies of each directive for Commission filing and State Department records.

subfiles.title: Filing Interim Directive Serial No. 100
subfiles.about: Files the certified U.S. interim directive on patent application priority.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Serial No. 100 for Commission records.

subfiles.title: Filing Directive Serial No. 101
subfiles.about: Files the certified directive on patents, utility models, and designs.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Serial No. 101 for Commission records.

subfiles.title: Revalidation and Restoration of Patents Owned by Foreign Nationals
subfiles.about: Forwards a SCAP press release and a Japanese pamphlet on foreign industrial property.
subfiles.summary: Reports that implementation instructions are expected and that a SCAP official considers the Japanese pamphlet factually correct.

subfiles.title: Patent Rights to Be Revalidated
subfiles.from: Far East Command Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Announces restoration of Allied patent rights and priority protection in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Describes restoration requests, royalties or term extensions, and a separate directive for priority applications.

subfiles.title: Industrial Property
subfiles.about: Surveys foreign industrial property rights in Japan before, during, and after the war.
subfiles.summary: Reviews treaty protection, wartime cancellation and licensing, SCAP restrictions, and problems posed by restoration and foreign investment. It reproduces Japan’s Wartime Law of Industrial Property and tabulates foreign-owned patents, utility models, designs, and trademarks registered in 1941. The pamphlet urges protection for Japanese users and eventual permission for Japanese patent applications abroad.

subfiles.title: Disposition of Japanese-Owned Patents Outside Japan
subfiles.about: Considers an agreement on Japanese-owned patents abroad after Soviet rejection of FEC 311.
subfiles.summary: Participants favor seeking SCAP concurrence and then agreement from FEC and other governments.

subfiles.title: Transmission of SCAP Restoration Procedures
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAPIN 1990 and an April 11 press release on Allied patent restoration.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the order affects about 5,000 rights and may encourage renewed foreign licensing and investment.

subfiles.title: Procedures for Restoration of Patents, Utility Models, and Designs to Allied Nationals
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Directs procedures for restoring Allied industrial property and granting wartime filing priority.
subfiles.summary: Defines eligible owners and loss dates, permits restoration, royalties or term extensions, and sets a one-year request period from May 1, 1949. It protects certain prior users through licenses, orders disclosure and an end to patent secrecy, and requires repeal of remaining wartime restrictions.

subfiles.title: Allied Nationals’ Patent Rights to Be Restored
subfiles.from: Far East Command Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Explains SCAP’s restoration order and its expected effect on foreign business in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Describes revalidation of roughly 5,000 rights, royalty and extension options, priority for wartime inventions, repeal of wartime law, and routes for owners seeking information.

subfiles.title: Patent Properties in Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP patent releases, restoration instructions, and a telegram on claims procedures.
subfiles.summary: Urges publicity because about 3,100 American-owned patents may be affected.

subfiles.title: Restoration Inquiry Procedure
subfiles.about: Reports how owners should begin restoration inquiries with the Civil Property Custodian.
subfiles.summary: Requests wide publicity before the filing deadline.

subfiles.title: Availability of Japanese Patent Records
subfiles.about: Asks whether the public can again obtain copies of prewar Japanese patents.
subfiles.summary: Describes difficulty obtaining wartime-seized patents for textile research.

subfiles.title: Reply on Japanese Patent Records
subfiles.about: Explains where to obtain copies of prewar and wartime Japanese patents.
subfiles.summary: Directs Rose to the U.S. Patent Office Scientific Library and notes plans to resume patent publication and exchange.

subfiles.title: Reference Slip on Patent Inquiry
subfiles.about: Records an internal note that a patent inquiry had been answered.
subfiles.summary: Notes an earlier reply and an extension number.

subfiles.title: Japanese Board of Patents Letter to U.S. Commissioner
subfiles.about: Forwards Japan’s request for information on Japanese applications in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the Board of Patents letter.

subfiles.title: Patent Inquiry for Romania
subfiles.about: Forwards Japan’s inquiry about Japanese patent, design, and trademark applications in Romania.
subfiles.summary: Requests delivery to the Romanian Patent Office if unobjectionable.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Fifteen Japanese Patent Office Letters
subfiles.about: Sends fifteen Japanese Board of Patents inquiries for onward delivery abroad.
subfiles.summary: Lists the intended patent offices and notes twenty-three similar letters already forwarded in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Treatment of Japanese Patents Outside Japan
subfiles.about: Seeks Justice Department views on a proposed international policy for Japanese patents abroad.
subfiles.summary: Notes that Soviet dissent prevented Commission approval and asks for an early reply.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on Revival of American-Owned Japanese Patents
subfiles.about: Asks where and how to petition for revival of a client’s Japanese patents.
subfiles.summary: Requests practical filing instructions for patents that lapsed during hostilities.

subfiles.title: Reply to Harvey M. Gillespie
subfiles.about: Provides restoration materials and filing information for American-owned Japanese patents.
subfiles.summary: Encloses press releases and a forthcoming Patent Office notice; clarifies that Japan’s Patent Office reopened in September 1948.
